import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

An app is a Rust library built into a `calimero:app` component. It declares
itself with the attributes `calimero-sdk` re-exports under `calimero_sdk::app`
(defined in `crates/sdk-macros`) and `#[derive(Record)]`. One import brings them
all in scope:

```rust
use calimero_sdk::prelude::*;
```

## Summary

| Attribute | On | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `#[app::state(version = N)]` | struct | The state root: tables and collections. |
| `#[app::logic]` | `impl` of the state | Every `pub fn` becomes a method; generates the `handle` export and the ABI. |
| `#[app::init]` | method | The constructor, run once when the app is created (as the owner). |
| `#[app::view]` | `&self` method | A read: runs as a view, never as a write. |
| `#[app::confirm]` | method | The caller confirms with a fresh passkey assertion. |
| `#[app::public]` / `#[app::public(rate = "10/min")]` | method | Callable without signing in (on a public app), optionally rate-limited. |
| `#[app::every("1m")]` | method | A timer the node runs on that interval (`<n>s`, `<n>m` or `<n>h`). |
| `#[app::allow(system)]` | method | The node itself may call it (implied by `every`). |
| `#[app::allow(app = "<id>")]` / `allow(app = "*")` | method | Another app may call it with a cross-app call. |
| `#[app::action]` | method | An action: may fetch over HTTP and read and call the app, outside the log. |
| `#[app::allow(action)]` | method | Only the app's own actions may call it. |
| `#[app::compute(fuel = .., result = "..")]` | method | A compute method: runs on a job node over sealed files, outside the log. |
| `#[app::compute_result]` | method | The logged call the node runs with a compute run's outcome. |
| `#[app::error]` | enum | The app's errors: variant name = error code. |
| `#[app::event]` | enum | The app's events: variant name = event name. |
| `#[derive(Record)]` + `#[table(..)]` | struct | A table row: key, unique constraints, indexes, counts, search. |
| `#[derive(AbiType)]` | serde struct or enum | Its JSON shape in the ABI's `types`, so typed clients get its fields. |
| `app::bail!(err)` | expression | Return early with an app error. |

## A complete app

The sample guest the SDK's own tests run (`crates/sdk/tests/guests/sample`),
shortened:

```rust
use calimero_sdk::prelude::*;

#[derive(Record)]
#[table(
    key = "id",
    unique(slot = ["room_id", "start"]),
    index(by_start = ["checked_in", "start"]),
    count(by_room = ["room_id"]),
)]
pub struct Booking {
    pub id: String,
    pub room_id: String,
    pub start: u64,
    pub title: String,
    pub checked_in: bool,
}

#[app::state(version = 3)]
pub struct Rooms {
    bookings: Table<Booking>,
    titles: UnorderedMap<String, String>,
    next_id: Counter,
}

#[app::error]
pub enum Error {
    NotFound,
    Taken { start: u64 },
    Invalid { reason: String },
}

#[app::event]
pub enum Event {
    Booked { id: String, room_id: String, start: u64 },
    Released { id: String },
}

#[app::logic]
impl Rooms {
    #[app::init]
    pub fn init() -> app::Result<Self> {
        Ok(Self::load())
    }

    pub fn book(&mut self, room_id: String, start: u64, title: String) -> app::Result<String> {
        if title.is_empty() {
            app::bail!(Error::Invalid { reason: "empty title".into() });
        }
        let id = env::unique_id();
        self.bookings.insert(Booking { id: id.clone(), room_id: room_id.clone(), start, title, checked_in: false })?;
        env::emit(Event::Booked { id: id.clone(), room_id, start }, Audience::All)?;
        Ok(id)
    }

    #[app::view]
    #[app::public]
    pub fn room_count(&self, room_id: String) -> app::Result<u64> {
        Ok(self.bookings.count("byRoom", &[KeyPart::Str(room_id)])?)
    }

    #[app::confirm]
    pub fn admin_release(&mut self, id: String) -> app::Result<()> {
        if !self.bookings.remove(&id)? {
            app::bail!(Error::NotFound);
        }
        env::emit(Event::Released { id }, Audience::All)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    #[app::every("30s")]
    pub fn heartbeat(&mut self) -> app::Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }
}
```

Compile-time refusals worth knowing: an `every` interval other than
`<n>s|m|h`, a `rate` other than `<n>/s|min|h`, `init` with any other attribute,
a `u64`/`i64`/`Vec<u8>` nested in another type the macro sees, and a table
`partition` (reserved).

## `#[app::state(version = N)]`

The struct holds handles only: each field is a [table or collection](/build/collections/),
built from its camelCase field name, so `Self::load()` reads nothing. `version`
is recorded in the ABI. The fields and their kinds (`table`, `unorderedMap`,
`counter`, `cell`, `set`, `vector`, `frozen`, `perUser`, `text`, `richText`) are
listed in the ABI too.

## `#[app::logic]`

On the state's `impl` block. Every `pub fn` is a method, named in camelCase in
the ABI (`room_count` → `roomCount`); private `fn`s stay helpers. A method's
receiver says its kind: `&mut self` is a call, `&self` with `#[app::view]` a
view, and `#[app::init]` has no receiver and returns `Self`. Every method,
`init` included, may take parameters, and every method returns `app::Result<T>`.

`init`'s parameters work like a call's: the node passes the app's `initArgs`
(`POST /apps`, `meroctl instance create --params`) as a JSON object keyed by the
camelCase parameter names, and the ABI lists them, so typed clients declare
them as `InitArgs` ([typed clients](/build/guides/typed-clients/)). A missing
required argument, a wrong type or an unknown name fails `init` with `BadArgs`,
and the create answers `422 INIT_FAILED`. Make a parameter an `Option` when
the app should also start without it:

```rust
#[app::init]
pub fn init(title: String, max_players: Option<u64>) -> app::Result<Self> {
    let mut app = Self::load();
    app.title.set(&title)?;
    app.max_players.set(&max_players.unwrap_or(2))?;
    Ok(app)
}
```

```bash
meroctl instance create --name blitz --package com.example.game --params '{"title":"Friday blitz","maxPlayers":"4"}'
```

The `u64` travels as a decimal string, as in any call.

The generated `handle`:

- **Arguments** are a JSON object keyed by camelCase parameter names; unknown
  keys are refused (`BadArgs`).
- **64-bit integers and bytes:** `u64`, `i64` and `Vec<u8>` (and `Option` of
  each) travel as decimal strings and base64url without padding, in arguments,
  results, record fields, and error and event fields, so no JavaScript client
  loses precision. The same types nested in another type the macro sees
  (`Vec<u64>`, `Option<Vec<i64>>`) are a compile error: wrap them in a `Record`
  or use a string.
- **Kinds:** a view may run as a call; a call run as a view is `NotAView`; an
  unknown method is `UnknownMethod`.
- **Callers** are checked after the kind: `allow(system)` admits the node,
  `allow(app = ..)` another app, `public` a caller who is not signed in.

## Method attributes

- `#[app::init]` runs once, as the owner, with the app's `initArgs`, and takes
  no other attribute.
- `#[app::view]` makes the method a read.
- `#[app::confirm]` asks the node to require a fresh passkey assertion for the
  call.
- `#[app::public]` lets a caller who is not signed in reach the method on a
  public app; `rate = "<n>/s|min|h"` limits it.
- `#[app::every("<n>s|m|h")]` is a timer. It implies `allow(system)`. Inside it,
  `env::timer()` gives the tick (`scheduled`, and `previous` when there was one).
- `#[app::allow(app = "<app id>")]`, or `"*"` for any app, admits
  [cross-app calls](/build/guides/cross-context/).
- `#[app::compute(fuel = N, memory_mib = M, wall_secs = S, result = "method")]`
  marks a compute method: no `self`, run on a job node from the app's compute
  component, with `fuel` and `result` required and the memory and wall caps
  optional (the host checks them against its maxima). `result` names an
  `#[app::compute_result]` method of the same block: a plain call method, not
  public, that implies `allow(system)` and takes the run's whole
  `ComputeOutcome` as its one parameter. A compute method takes no other kind
  or access attribute. See [Compute actions](/build/guides/compute-actions/).
- `#[app::action]` takes no `self`; its first parameter is
  `ctx: &mut ActionCtx`, with `ctx.view`, `ctx.call` and `ctx.fetch` (see
  [Outbound](/build/guides/outbound/)). `#[app::allow(action)]` on a method
  lets only the app's own actions call it.

## `#[app::error]` and `#[app::event]`

Both go in the `#[app::logic]` module, at most one of each. Every field has a
name: a tuple variant (`Invalid(String)`), or a tuple struct in place of the
enum, is a compile error; unit variants are fine.

- `#[app::error]` implements `From<Error> for AppError`. The variant name is the
  code; the fields become the error's `message`, a JSON object with camelCase
  keys (`Taken { start: 7 }` → code `Taken`, `{"start":"7"}`). A client sees
  it as `422 APP_ERROR` with `details.code` and `details.fields`.
- `#[app::event]` implements `AppEvent`, emitted with
  `env::emit(event, audience)` (see [Events](/build/guides/events/)).

`app::bail!(Error::NotFound)` returns `Err(Error::NotFound.into())`.

## `#[derive(Record)]` and `#[table(..)]`

A table row. The derive writes the serde impls itself, so do not also derive
`Serialize`/`Deserialize` on the record.

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `key = "field"` | The primary key. |
| `unique(name = ["f", ..])` | A unique constraint; an insert that breaks it fails. |
| `index(name = ["f", ..])` | An index, read with `Table::find`. |
| `count(name = ["f", ..])` | A count kept on every write, read with `Table::count`. |
| `search = ["f", ..]` | Fields indexed for [full-text search](/build/guides/search/). |

Index, count and unique names are used in camelCase (`by_room` → `"byRoom"`).
`u64`/`i64` fields are CBOR integers when stored and decimal strings in JSON.
A record's fields are listed in the ABI's `types` too, so a
[typed client](/build/guides/typed-clients/) types it as an interface.

## `#[derive(AbiType)]`

A record describes itself in the ABI. A plain serde type a method takes or
answers (a view of several records, a status enum, a generic page) does so when
it also derives `AbiType`:

```rust
#[derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, AbiType)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct Listing<T> {
    pub items: Vec<T>,
    pub next_cursor: Option<String>,
    #[serde(with = "calimero_sdk::json::u64_str")]
    pub total: u64,
}

#[derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, AbiType)]
#[serde(tag = "state", rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub enum Slot {
    Free,
    Held { booking: Booking },
}
```

It reads the serde attributes that change the JSON (`rename`, `rename_all`,
`rename_all_fields`, `tag`, `content`, `untagged`, `transparent`, `skip`,
`skip_serializing_if`, `default`) and refuses what it cannot describe: `flatten`, `into`,
`from`, `try_from`, `remote`, and a `with` other than the SDK's D20 helpers. A
field `skip_serializing_if` may leave out, or `#[serde(default)]` (on the field, or
on the struct for every field) lets a caller leave out, is optional in the shape, so
generated argument types do not require it.

A `u64`, `i64` or `Vec<u8>` field says which JSON it travels as. Either it names
its D20 helper (`json::u64_str`, `i64_str`, `bytes_b64url`, or their `opt_`
forms: a decimal string, base64url), or it is marked `#[abi(plain)]` and keeps
what plain serde writes, described as such: `u64_number` / `i64_number` (a JSON
number) and `byte_list` (an array of numbers), at any depth (`Vec<u64>`,
`Option<i64>`). `#[abi(plain)]` on the struct or enum marks every field; a D20
`with` on a field still wins. Unmarked, the field is refused: the ABI's `u64` and
`bytes` mean the strings.

```rust
#[derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, AbiType)]
pub struct ShotsView {
    #[abi(plain)]
    pub shots: Vec<u8>, // [3, 17, ...]: `byte_list`
    #[abi(plain)]
    pub updated_at: u64, // 1700000000000: `u64_number`
    #[serde(default)]
    pub note: Option<String>, // a caller may leave it out
}
```

A JSON number past 2^53 loses precision in JavaScript (the TypeScript client types
`u64_number` as `number`), so `#[abi(plain)]` suits values that stay below it
(timestamps in milliseconds, counts) or apps whose JSON is already fixed; a new
field is better as D20's string. A type without
either derive stays in the ABI by name only, and clients type it `unknown`.
Two mutually recursive described types do not compile (a type that contains
itself does); describe one of them by hand (`impl AbiType`) or not at all.

## The SDK's name

The crate is `calimero-sdk`. Its old name, `calimero-app-sdk`, still works while
apps move over: it re-exports `calimero-sdk`, and the attributes expand to paths
through whichever name the app's `Cargo.toml` lists (or the name a renamed
dependency gives it).

<Aside type="note">
  Not in this version: migrations between state versions (`#[app::migrate]`),
  event handlers and typed index enums. See [Migrations](/build/migrations/).
</Aside>
